evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 形義通解；字形分析與用例
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 星 as 从晶、生聲: 晶 depicts an array of stars and 生 is the phonetic. It reports the original sense as stars, a Western Zhou bronze inscription 麓伯簋 using 星 in a personal name, and an oracle-bone example 合集15625反 read as “晴” (clear weather). It also cites 星言夙駕 in the Shijing as clear-weather use, but that interpretation is disputed. The entry records later borrowing of 星 for 腥 in Warring States/Qin slips and Han silk manuscripts, and extensions such as scattered or numerous. These attestations do not establish a precise first-occurrence date for each sense.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：甲骨部件分析—晶

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.text: The entry quotes the Shuowen analysis 从晶，生聲 and its alternative pictographic explanation, then treats 晶 as an earlier spelling for the star word. It also describes later 晶 senses such as bright, clear, and crystal. This is the dictionary's historical interpretation; the detailed sequence is not settled by the text alone.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：甲骨部件分析—晶

evidence.source: 《說文解字》, transcribed in the CUHK historical dictionary entry
evidence.text: The entry identifies 生 as 星's phonetic component. The supplied local Baxter–Sagart rows (sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv; rows for 星 and 生) give 星 MC seng, OC *s-tsʰˤeŋ and 生 MC sraeng, OC *sreŋ (with listed variants/notes). Those same-system local rows show a sound relationship to assess, but do not independently prove the historical phonetic function. The official reconstruction-table PDF could not be opened in this session. Supplied local Unihan rows (sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt; kMandarin rows for 星 and 生) give xīng and shēng; official per-character Unicode pages could not be inspected, so these values are not asserted as externally verified here.

evidence.source: 國學大師字形演變 compilation
evidence.text: The page catalogs oracle-bone forms, a Western Zhou bronze inscription, Warring States forms, seal forms, and later scripts. Its explanation says the two displayed oracle-bone examples combine a star depiction with 生, while some Warring States forms simplify 晶 and retain 生 as phonetic; it describes reduction of the star depiction to 日. This account differs from the attached 《說文新證》 note on another inspected page, which says a 晶-only form preceded the addition of 生. The text view does not resolve whether these concern different early forms or competing analyses; no glyph image was visually inspected in this pass.

Early graphic development remains disputed in the inspected accounts: whether a 晶-only spelling preceded 星 with 生, or whether oracle-bone forms already include a star depiction plus 生. Glyph images were not visually inspected, and no corruption claim is established.
The earliest cited oracle-bone example interpreted as clear weather and the Shijing phrase have interpretive uncertainty. No securely dated first occurrence of each sense is established here.

Later uses for scattered/many, clear weather, and graph borrowing for 腥 are recorded as distinct claims; this pass did not independently establish a complete semantic chronology or all links between senses.
The attempted external search results and opened pages do not establish an independent pronunciation for the depicted star object; no whole-graph phonetic-loan claim is made.
